To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
single cell RNA sequencing identified Yes-associated protein  1 (YAP) as the key driver of proliferation in fibrolamella r carcinoma (FLC), which may be therapeutically targeted.

single cell RNA sequencing of FLC identifies YAP1-driven mesothelial progeny as the source of both epithelial and stromally derived FLC cells, and inhibition of YAP1 reduces FLC cell growth and migration, identifying YAP as a potential target for FLC treatment.

single-cell transcriptomic analysis of a patient-derived xenograft model of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma revealed that both the FLC epithelial tumor cells and the stromal fibrotic cells arise from a single cell of origin, a YAP1-positive mesothelial progeny, and inhibition of YAP1 in FLC cells significantly reduces cell growth, cell migration, and the expression of known YAPI target genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cell of origin for fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma, a rare liver cancer.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FLC)
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for FLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
YAP1 is a therapeutic target for FLC, but it is not clear whether the DNAJB1/PRKACA fusion is the driver or YAP1 activation.
the authors have identified YAP1 as an important driver of FLC growth and progression, and that targeting this pathway may have clinical benefit in this disease.
the YAP1-dependent mesothelial progenitior cell type may be a novel target for FLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a YAP1 dependent mesothelial progeny that can give rise to both the tumor and the stromal components of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma.
we identified a YAP1 dependent hepatic mesothelium progenitor cell that is the origin for both the epithelial and stromatic components of FLC.
FLC cells arise from YAP1-dependent mesothelial progeny, which can be inhibited by YAP1 inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNAJB1/PRKACA fusion is not sufficient to drive FLC tumorigenesis and that YAP1 is required for FLC cell survival.
the YAP1 pathway is a potential therapeutic target for FLC.
YAP1 inhibition can be used to treat FLC.
